protection.title: Web Protection
protection.description: Managed rules, custom rules and rate limiting for this site.
protection.performanceHint: Higher interception rate at a proportional performance cost.

protection.monitorExplainer: A switched-on downgrade keeps detection fully active but records instead of blocking. Language-agnostic detections are never downgraded by a stack switch.

protection.underAttackActiveHint: All visitors are challenged. Turn it off once the attack subsides.

categories.linkageHint: Managed rules of this family follow this switch; switching back resets their individual toggles.

managedRules.cardHint: Downgrade built-in rules one by one, or flip the whole set with the batch buttons.

caching.purgeAllDescription: This evicts every cached object for the site. This cannot be undone.

caching.activationSwitchHint: Rules keep their own switches; this one flips all of them together.

caching.disableDescription: {{count}} rules were turned off; the rules themselves are kept.

caching.limitsEffectiveHint: Effective cap = min(global, site, type): currently {{effective}} MiB.

ssl.caOrganizationHint: Optional. Certificate requests from this CA must carry this organization.
ssl.caEmptyDescription: Add or import a CA to start verifying client certificates.
ssl.caDeleteDescription: Clients holding certificates from this CA will no longer be trusted. A CA that still signed certificates must have them revoked and deleted first.
ssl.clientCertsHint: Certificates issued by this site's CAs. Revoking one rejects it at the edge.
ssl.issueCertHint: The client keeps the private key; the edge only accepts certificates that chain to a CA above.

ssl.certOrganizationHint: Defaults to the CA's expected organization.

ssl.deleteCertDescription: This removes the record and, with it, the stored private key. Revoked certificates only.
ssl.emptyClientCertsDescription: Issue a certificate from a generated CA to hand out to a client.

ssl.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard — download the bundle instead.
ssl.issueElsewhereHint: Certificates are issued, uploaded and renewed on the global SSL/TLS page.

lifecycle.title: Request lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Where every PingWAF feature acts in the proxy pipeline. Use this map to see which stage your WAF, IP, bot, rate-limit and cache rules run in, and to debug why a request was allowed, blocked or challenged.

tls.title: TLS & connection
tls.desc: The TLS handshake happens before any HTTP processing: SNI selects the certificate, and when any site enables mTLS the listener verifies client certificates against the union of trusted CAs (per-site enforcement runs in the WAF plugin).

earlyRequest.title: Early request
earlyRequest.desc: The location (host + path) is matched and the request context is created, then every early_request plugin runs: the WAF plugin's full check chain (below) and the challenge verify endpoint /_pingwaf/challenge/verify. A plugin answering here short-circuits every later stage.

request.title: Request
request.desc: ACME HTTP-01 and metrics requests are answered here (after passing the WAF above), then the location path rewrite and request-step plugins run: the rewrite plugin and the cache plugin (per-session cache setup, PURGE handling). A request matching no location gets a 404 without running any plugin.

cacheLookup.title: Cache lookup
cacheLookup.desc: Pingora's built-in HTTP cache. A hit ends the request without contacting the upstream — but the request already passed the WAF and rewrite. A miss continues to the upstream.

upstream.title: Upstream
upstream.desc: The load balancer picks a backend (with retries on connect failure), X-Forwarded-* style headers are appended, and the body is streamed upstream; oversized bodies are rejected with 413.

upstreamResponse.title: Upstream response
upstreamResponse.desc: The upstream response headers arrive: pingora decides whether the response may be stored in the cache, and the error page plugin can replace upstream error responses (400+, including 502/504) with the site's custom pages.

response.title: Response
response.desc: Response-step plugins run: the WAF plugin records status and size for the access log, the per-site HSTS plugin adds Strict-Transport-Security, and cache headers (Age, …) are added. Response body filters then rewrite the body — except after a 101 upgrade, where the bytes are WebSocket traffic.

responseBody.title: Response body
responseBody.desc: At end of stream the WAF plugin emits the access log entry (with the response body sampled per the site's logging settings).

failure.title: Failure
failure.desc: Only on errors: classified as 502 upstream error / 499 client gone / 408 read timeout / 400 invalid header, then rendered with pingap's built-in error template. No plugin runs here, so custom error pages cannot replace this page.

logging.title: Logging
logging.desc: pingap writes its own access log last. PingWAF's entries were already emitted at the stage where the decision was made: generated responses (blocks, challenges, pause pages) at request time, regular responses when the body completes.

lifecycle.wafDescription: The checks run in this order on every request; the first one that answers ends the request.

paused.title: Paused site
paused.desc: A paused site answers with the pause page immediately — nothing else runs.

mtls.title: mTLS client certificate
mtls.desc: A missing or invalid client certificate is blocked at the site level.

access.title: IP & geo rules
access.desc: First match wins (priority ascending). Actions: block, allow, challenge, js_challenge — or basic_auth, deferred to the next check.

basicAuth.title: Basic Auth
basicAuth.desc: Site-wide or triggered by an IP/geo rule. Failed attempts get a small delay; unauthenticated requests get the 401 page. hide_credentials strips the Authorization header.

bot.title: Bot protection
bot.desc: User-agent classification: pass, deny (block page) or log only.

rateLimit.title: Rate limiting
rateLimit.desc: Fixed-window counters per rule (IP, host, path, header, cookie…). Over the threshold the rule's action runs; challenge can issue a clearance cookie.

engine.title: WAF engine
engine.desc: Signature and expression rules with an anomaly score. Verdicts: pass, monitor (log only), block, challenge.

lifecycle.tipsDescription: Common questions answered by the lifecycle order.

observation.title: Observation mode
observation.desc: Detections keep running but block/challenge verdicts are only recorded as "would have blocked". Paused sites, mTLS and Basic Auth are still enforced.

firstMatch.title: Order matters
firstMatch.desc: IP and geo rules evaluate top-down and the first match wins — an allow rule above a catch-all block decides the outcome.

cache.title: Cache never bypasses the WAF
cache.desc: Checks run before the cache lookup, so cached hits are inspected like any other request, and a block always wins over a cached response.

customPages.title: Custom error pages
customPages.desc: Error pages replace upstream error responses. WAF block/challenge pages are generated before the upstream is contacted and keep their built-in design.

responseCache.title: Response edits and the cache
responseCache.desc: The cache stores the response as it leaves the upstream phase. Response-phase changes — rewrite response rules, HSTS — run after the cache on every serve (cache hits included), so the stored copy stays unmodified; error-page replacements are sent with no-store and never stored.

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: Manage origin pools, load balancing, route dispatch and trusted proxy settings.
basic.poolCreateDescription: An origin pool is a set of origin nodes sharing one load-balancing algorithm and origin protocol.
basic.poolEditDescription: Change the pool's load-balancing algorithm or origin protocol.
basic.poolsEmptyDescription: Create an origin pool to hold your origin nodes.
basic.nodesEmptyDescription: An empty pool cannot serve traffic — add an origin node.
basic.nodeDialogDescription: A node is an origin address that receives proxied traffic.
basic.nodeAddressHint: IP or hostname plus optional port, e.g. http://10.0.0.1:8080. A pasted scheme is dropped; paths are not allowed.
basic.nodeWeightHint: 1-10000; round robin splits traffic by weight
basic.lbHint: Round robin spreads by weight; hash pins similar requests to one node
basic.lbKeyHint: Header / cookie / query parameter name to hash on
basic.httpsOriginHint: Connect to the origin over TLS; requires the hostname on its certificate.
basic.sniHint: Hostname covered by the origin certificate; $host is not supported
basic.verifyCertHint: "Follow the site setting" first checks this site's origin certificate check (SSL page), then falls back to Settings → Origin TLS verification; pinning a value here fixes it for this pool.
basic.healthCheckHint: Probe origins periodically: nodes with consecutive failures are removed and added back on recovery. Recommended for multi-node pools.
basic.healthCheckPathHint: Starts with '/', no spaces, '?' or '#', e.g. /healthz
basic.healthCheckIntervalHint: 5-3600; aligned up to the agent's 10s grid (15 -> 20)
basic.healthCheckUnhealthyHint: Consecutive failures before a node is marked unhealthy, 1-10
basic.healthCheckHealthyHint: Consecutive successes before a node recovers, 1-10
basic.routesDescription: Dispatch requests to different pools by path; unmatched traffic goes to the default pool.
basic.routesEmptyDescription: All traffic currently goes to the default pool; add a route to split it by path.
basic.routeDialogDescription: Requests whose path matches the rule are forwarded to the target pool.
basic.priorityHint: 1-60000; empty uses the auto weight (exact 1024 / prefix 512 / regex 256)
basic.ipGroupHint: Only clients inside the group match this route; other clients fall through to the next route.
basic.deletePoolDescription: This cannot be undone; remove its nodes and route references first.
basic.deleteNodeDescription: The origin address will no longer receive traffic.
basic.deleteRouteDescription: Matching traffic will fall back to the default pool.

proxyTrust.title: Trusted Proxy
proxyTrust.description: When the site sits behind a CDN or reverse proxy, the client IP is resolved from a trusted header; IP blocks, CC rules and access logs all key on it.
proxyTrust.enabledHint: Resolve the client IP from the header below instead of the TCP peer
proxyTrust.lastHopHint: Take only the last X-Forwarded-For entry (appended by the closest proxy, cannot be spoofed by clients) and ignore the rest
proxyTrust.groupsHint: Ranges of the selected groups merge with the manual entries below into one trust scope — e.g. the built-in Cloudflare group tracks Cloudflare's edge network automatically.
proxyTrust.effectiveRanges: Effective scope: {{count}} CIDR ranges (union of manual entries and selected groups).
proxyTrust.effectiveEmpty: Effective scope: empty — no forwarded header is trusted at all.
proxyTrust.rangesHint: One CIDR (or bare IP) per line. Only direct peers inside these ranges may set the trusted header — leave empty and no forwarded header is trusted at all.
proxyTrust.rangesInvalid: One of the ranges is not a valid CIDR or IP address
proxyTrust.headerHint: Only valid IP values are accepted; resolution falls back to the peer address on failure
